lead: Nalanda was a giant school-monastery in Bihar, India, where monks studied for about seven hundred years. This page rebuilds the water clock that ran their day, and checks which famous stories about Nalanda the old records really support.
try: In “The water clock that ran the day”, drag the Day of the year slider from summer to winter and watch how long Each sinking of the bowl takes. Turn on Drum sound to hear the drum mark the hours.
points: The clock was a small copper bowl with a tiny hole, floating in water. Each time it filled and sank, someone struck a drum.
The bowl sank 32 times in a full day and night. Daytime hours were longer in summer than in winter, so the hole had to change with the seasons.
Some popular claims, like Nalanda having 10,000 students, go beyond what the eyewitnesses wrote, so every claim on the page is tagged as evidence, an eyewitness number, or legend.
